newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises par of 3-, 6-mth T-bill offers.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises par of 3-, 6-mth T-bill offers.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry raised the total par on offer for Monday's auctions of three-and six-montn discount T-bills nearly three-fold in a bid to boost secondary trade, a central bank official said on Friday.

"The par on offer was raised to compensate the lower par of four-week discount offers and in a bid to activate trade on the secondary market," Nikolina Micheva, head of State Credits department at the central bank told Reuters.
The total par value of the issues, to be offered with no minimum acceptable price set in advance, was raised to 45 billion levs from 16 billion levs at this week's auction.
The Finance Ministry pared the par of four-week discount T-bill issues to be offered at daily auctions next week to 10 billion levs each from 15 billion levs this week.
The ministry will halt those issues from June 30 in favour of longer maturities in a bid to ease domestic debt servicing.
Offering fewer issues with higher par value was in line with Finance Ministry's aim to let more institutions qualify at the auctions and boost secondary trade in government securities.
Par value 25 bln levs 20 bln levs
